title: Decoding the CBDT's Expanded 'Specified Fund' Definition: A Game-Changer for AIFs in India and GIFT City
content:
# Decoding the CBDT's Expanded 'Specified Fund' Definition: A Game-Changer for AIFs in India and GIFT City As tax and legal professionals, we often find ourselves navigating a labyrinth of rules and regulations, especially when it comes to the dynamic world of investment funds. Just when you think you've got a handle on things, a new amendment comes along, bringing both clarity and a fresh set of considerations. Well, **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** has recently done just that, with a significant amendment to the **Income-tax Rules, 2026**, specifically expanding the definition of ‘Specified Fund’. This isn't just a technical tweak; it's a strategic move with profound implications for Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) regulated by SEBI and the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA). Effective from July 21, 2026, this change aims to bring greater alignment and certainty, especially for funds operating in our aspiring global financial hub, GIFT City. Let’s dive deep into what this amendment entails and why it matters. ### The 'What': Unpacking the CBDT's Latest Notification The Ministry of Finance, through the CBDT, has issued the **Income-tax (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026**, vide Notification No. G.S.R. 646(E) [F. No. 370142/24/2026-TPL] on July 21, 2026. This notification substitutes clause (c) of sub-rule (5) of Rule 157 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, thereby revising the definition of a "specified fund". The amendment came into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette on the same day. Before this amendment, while the concept of 'specified fund' was crucial for various tax treatments, its exact contours, especially concerning the relatively newer IFSCA-regulated entities and a specific reference to the Income-tax Act, 2025, needed streamlining. Now, the definition is much more comprehensive and explicit. ### The 'Why': A Strategic Move for Clarity and Growth What was the driving force behind this amendment? In simpler terms, it was about providing much-needed clarity and fostering growth in India's investment landscape. The primary objectives are multi-fold: * **Alignment with the Income-tax Act, 2025:** The amendment ensures that the Income-tax Rules are in harmony with the broader framework introduced under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This legislative synchronization is vital for a stable and predictable tax regime. * **Promoting International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs):** With GIFT City emerging as a significant global financial hub, the government is keen to provide a conducive environment for funds operating there. Explicitly including IFSCA-regulated funds within the 'specified fund' definition offers regulatory certainty and boosts confidence for funds located in an IFSC. This, in turn, helps in strengthening India's position as a global investment destination. * **Enhancing Tax Compliance and Classification:** By broadening the categories of investment funds that qualify as 'specified funds,' the CBDT aims to improve tax compliance and ensure clearer classification of funds eligible for various tax benefits. This step is a big relief for fund managers and investors alike. * **Streamlining Investment Vehicles:** The amendment acknowledges the evolving nature of investment structures and aims to ensure that a wider array of legitimate investment vehicles can avail appropriate tax treatments without ambiguity. ### Old Provision vs. New Provision: What Exactly Has Changed? Let's look at the heart of the amendment – the revised definition of a "specified fund" under **Rule 157(5)(c)**. | Feature | Old Provision (Implied Scope) | New Provision (As per Notification G.S.R. 646(E)) | | :------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Legal Structure** | Likely covered funds established or incorporated in India as a trust, company, LLP, or body corporate. | Explicitly includes any fund established or incorporated in India in the form of a **trust, company, limited liability partnership (LLP), or body corporate**. | | **AIF Registration** | Focused primarily on **Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)** registered under SEBI regulations. | Must hold a certificate of registration as a **Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF)**. | | **Regulatory Framework** | Primarily regulated under **SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012**. | Must be regulated under either:
(A) The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012** (made under the SEBI Act, 1992); OR
(B) The **International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022** (made under the IFSCA Act, 2019), *and* which is located in any **International Financial Services Centre (IFSC)**. | | **Statutory Reference** | Less explicit or did not specifically refer to newer provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025. | Also explicitly includes **any fund which has been referred to in Schedule VI [Note 1(g)] to the Income-tax Act, 2025**. | | **Scope of Application** | More limited, potentially leading to ambiguity for funds in IFSCs or those linked to specific new provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025. | **Expanded**, providing clear recognition for both SEBI and IFSCA-regulated Category I and II AIFs, and aligning with specific statutory references in the Income-tax Act, 2025. This removes a lot of *khichdi* (confusion) that might have existed earlier. | ### The Impact: What Does This Mean for You? This expanded definition has several significant implications for the Indian financial ecosystem: * **Boost for GIFT City:** For funds establishing or already operating in an IFSC like GIFT City, this amendment is a shot in the arm. By explicitly recognizing IFSCA-regulated funds as 'specified funds', it paves the way for them to unequivocally avail various tax incentives and benefits associated with this classification. This is crucial for attracting more capital and fund management activities to India's first operational smart city. * **Clarity for AIFs and Investors:** AIFs, particularly Category I and II, typically enjoy a 'pass-through' status, meaning income is taxed at the investor level, not at the fund level (with some exceptions like business income for Category II AIFs). This clarity in definition ensures that a broader range of legitimate funds can confidently operate under this beneficial tax structure. For investors, this translates into reduced uncertainty about the tax treatment of their investments in these funds. * **Harmonization of Laws:** The explicit inclusion of funds referred to in Schedule VI [Note 1(g)] of the Income-tax Act, 2025, demonstrates the government's commitment to creating a cohesive legal framework. This harmonization reduces potential conflicts and ensures consistency between the Act and the Rules. * **Ease of Doing Business (Thoda Aur Aasan Hua!):** When definitions are clear, compliance becomes simpler. Fund managers and legal teams spend less time interpreting ambiguous provisions, allowing them to focus more on core investment activities. This promotes an environment of 'ease of doing business' for sophisticated investment vehicles. * **Enhanced Global Competitiveness:** By aligning our domestic tax regulations with global best practices, especially concerning international financial centers, India enhances its attractiveness as a destination for global capital. This amendment is a testament to the government’s vision to make India a competitive player in the global financial market. ### Concluding Thoughts The CBDT's latest amendment to the definition of 'specified fund' is a thoughtful and forward-looking step. It's a clear signal that the government is committed to refining our tax laws to support the growth of alternative investment funds and to position India, particularly its IFSCs, as a preferred global financial gateway. For fund houses, legal advisors, and investors, this enhanced clarity is a welcome development, offering a more stable and predictable regulatory landscape. While the devil, as always, will be in the details of implementation and future interpretations, this amendment definitely lays a stronger foundation. ## Read the Official Document * [Download the Official Notification/Circular here](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/latest-news-updates/notification-no-94-2026) *Published on: 26 July 2026*
